test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All anklets are printers.

Some printers are birds.

Some birds are cherries.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some birds are printers.

II. All printers are anklets.

III. Some cherries are birds.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follow.

solution:
Statements:

All anklets are printers.

Some printers are birds.

Some birds are cherries.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3e7337a46cdb875fed17da2eea5b7e483b72fc770517dc09ed8c796b79d052f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some birds are printers ⇒ True (As Some printers are birds so, from the above Venn diagram we can conclude that some birds are printers.)

II. All printers are anklets.⇒ False (As all anklets are printers but vice-versa is not true in a definite sense.)

III. Some cherries are birds ⇒True (As Some birds are cherries so, from the above Venn diagram we can conclude that Some cherries are birds.)

Hence, "**Both conclusions I and III follow". **
